A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same SNMF research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original concept-detection, causal-steering and neuron-compositionality experiments, including intervention results in Table 2 and additional appendix analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds initialization and sparsity comparisons, quantitative hierarchy results, and human–LLM judgment agreement.

M1.justification: The SNMF factorization, multiplicative updates, sparsification, residual-stream mapping and recursive decomposition remain unchanged. Alternative initializations and sparsity levels are evaluated as experimental variants; they do not replace the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions cover concept detection, steering and compositional hierarchies using the same kinds of generated concept and time-unit data. The 50-noun, 873-sentence ConceptNet-based construction described in v2 Appendix G already appears in v1 Appendix F.3. The additions expand analyses within existing coverage.

E2.justification: The main SAE and DiffMeans comparators are retained. V2 Table 8 adds a random-feature control for hierarchy evaluation. Its precise construction is ambiguous: Appendix G describes replacing parents, whereas the caption describes randomly pairing children.

E3.justification: V2 adds substantial evaluation protocols: initialization and sparsity sweeps, a two-level hierarchy test with ranks 500 and 200, a 2.5% linkage threshold, 20 prompts and top-token coverage metrics, plus a balanced 50-example human–LLM agreement check. These supplement the retained main benchmark protocols.

E4.justification: V2 adds initialization robustness, convergence-speed and sparsity analyses in Tables 3–7. Appendix G quantitatively tests parent–child causal relationships against a random control across two models, extending the earlier illustrative hierarchy analyses. The human judgment check also adds validation of the evaluation procedure.

E5.justification: V2 explicitly reports means and standard deviations in its new tables and adds a Spearman agreement estimate with significance reporting: rho = 0.8, p < 10^-4. Neither version establishes an increase in repeated runs or seeds.

E6.justification: Substantial new results appear in Tables 3–8. Table 5 reports mean convergence iterations of 1484 for K-means, 2474 for SVD and 3325 for random initialization. Table 8 reports hierarchy coverage of 0.46 versus 0.05 for Llama and 0.37 versus 0.00 for Gemma against the reported random control. Human–LLM agreement is also newly reported; the central benchmark conclusions and Table 2 values are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix G introduces mathematical definitions for parent–child linkage, coverage of children's promoted-token sets, diversity and mean coverage per child. The SNMF equations, cosine-versus-projection derivation and recursive reconstruction objective are retained; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the claims that SNMF discovers interpretable neuron combinations, supports effective causal steering and reveals compositional hierarchies. The new title and additional supporting experiments do not materially redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning initialization robustness, sparsity tradeoffs and systematic hierarchy structure rather than decomposition artifacts. The limitations replace the untested-initialization discussion with human–LLM agreement and prompt-sensitivity qualifications, while retaining scaling and optimizer limitations. Appendix E.1 also explains the adaptation of AxBench.

D1.justification: V2 documents the new hierarchy test's ranks, linkage threshold, prompt count and token-selection procedure, and explains the existing benchmark adaptation. Appendix C changes the second SAE architecture's description from Gated to L1-regularized while retaining its listed hyperparameter grid and budget; a rerun is not established. Code-access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations on neuron composition, attribution, concept factorization, prompt tuning and matrix-factorization scaling, including Mu and Andreas, Oikarinen and Weng, Fel and colleagues, and Mairal and colleagues. It removes Sajjad et al. and refines the comparison with Yun et al. The overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: V2 changes the title, edits several explanatory and related-work paragraphs, and rewrites the limitations. It expands Appendix E, adds a hierarchy-analysis appendix and moves the unchanged prompt appendix from G to H. The main section sequence and much of the prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 3–8 and makes localized presentation changes: Figure 2 becomes vertically stacked, Table 1 is shortened and loses its layer column, Figure 3 styling changes, and Figure 4 is redrawn vertically. The remaining appendix plots and hierarchy diagrams retain their content.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens support for existing claims through parameter checks addressing v1's initialization limitation, broader quantitative hierarchy validation, and a human check of LLM judging. These provide a clear empirical benefit. The inconsistent random-control descriptions in Appendix G and Table 8, together with limited human-evaluation procedural details, constrain the strength and reproducibility of the added validation.
